edits.old: Benchmark quantization on representative embeddings and queries before choosing it: independent embedding experiments and vector-engine documentation show that quality depends on model and data, and that rescoring can recover quality while adding retrieval work. Those results do not establish a MongoDB-specific recall guarantee. (high confidence)
edits.new: Benchmark quantization on representative embeddings and queries before choosing it: the Hugging Face embedding-quantization experiments show that quantization quality depends on the calibration data (and the model evaluated), and that rescoring recovers quality; MongoDB's Vector Search benchmark documentation shows that rescoring with full-fidelity vectors adds cost (reduced throughput at high concurrency) and recommends testing on a sample data set. Sources: https://huggingface.co/blog/embedding-quantization ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-vector-search/benchmark/results/

evidence.quote: It is important to note that the calibration dataset greatly influences performance since it defines the quantization buckets.
With binary embeddings, mxbai-embed-large-v1 retains 92.53% of performance on MTEB Retrieval. Just doing the rescoring without retrieving more samples pushes the performance to 96.45%.
The additional cost of rescoring for binary quantization shows up in reduced throughput when running highly concurrent workloads.
though we recommend running tests on the sample data set to ensure the performance fits your needs.

edits.rationale: The Hugging Face post shows rescoring recovers retained performance (92.53% to 96.45% for binary) and that the calibration dataset greatly influences scalar quantization. The extra retrieval work from rescoring comes from MongoDB's own benchmark page, not the HF post, so the source set needs that page added. The 'no MongoDB-specific recall guarantee' sentence is a scope disclaimer, not a checkable assertion, and was left out of the corrected text.
